text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Two joint Home Affairs Ministry raids night spots over weekend net more than 50 arrests on drugs, gambling, under-age drinking and other charges.
- Albanian President Sali Berisha does not want to resign despite anarchy enveloping country.
- About 730 flats in Tampines Court and Amberville estates to be privatised.
- NTUC Chief Lim Boon Heng says Singapore and Malaysia mutually dependent on each other.
- Property agents blame the introduction of executive condominiums for causing drop in sales of HUDC (government-subsidised) flats over the last few months.
- In survey by Political & Economic Risk Consultancy, Singapore takes second position after Hong Kong.
- More Asian companies buying into Japanese firms to acquire their technology.
- DBS Land announces 31 percent increase in net profit, making Singapore $207.3 million last year.
- World's financial system seriously at risk from structural faults in offshore banking system, according to leaked document from Bank for International Settlements, London newspaper says.
- Homegrown motor firm Stuttgart Auto eyes joint venture with Porsche Ag and Salim-linked Indomobil for assembly and distribution.
- Ossia International chairman plans to develop its newly-formed property arm into a core business.
- United Overseas Bank's Malaysia fund management seeks licence to manage domestic unit trust funds.
